title: Baroque Dancing Lesson 3 - Temps de Courante

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: Lesley Strachan provides clear verbal explanations combined with slow full-body demonstrations, often using imagery to aid understanding. She guides students through both front-facing and back-facing demonstrations to ensure all angles of the step are visible.

lesson_structure.note: Welcomes viewers and introduces lesson 3 on the temps de courante step
Breaks down mechanics holding onto a cupboard for balance
Demonstrates the step slowly counting out loud from the front
Demonstrates the exercise from the back view
Explains why she calls it the carrot step and concludes

cues: Rise onto the ball of the foot
metaphors: Pulling the carrot out of the floor
common_mistakes: Bending legs when up on the demi point

steps_taught.name: Temps de Courante
steps_taught.description: Rising to demi-plie/demi-point, sliding and straightening legs into first position

what_works: Showing the exercise from both front and back views
Breaking down counts slowly with verbal prompts
what_hinders: Dancing in a restricted domestic space without background contrast

quotes.text: Today we're going to do lesson three which is learning the tour de courante step.
We have to make sure that we have both legs straight and it's not bent.
I call the tour de courante my carrot step.

evidence_segments.observation: Teacher speaks to camera introducing the lesson topic.
Teacher holds a piece of furniture for balance while demonstrating demi-plié and rising on the ball of the foot.
evidence_segments.cannot_infer: exact weight distribution on the floor

extraction.distinctive_method: Labeling the step 'the carrot step' to create a mental image of pulling something up from the floor.
